brief: AI exposure has crowded out every other market narrative, including the trade used to escape it. US and European defensives just posted record outperformance (US staples' best month since October 2000, European defensives' best spread versus the market since 1997) as investors rotated out of the AI pain trade. Goldman's Wilson also finds the 10-year Treasury yield now correlates about 0.6 with AI-related equities, versus a flipped-negative correlation with Brent, so the bond market reads an AI selloff as a growth scare. Goldman's Miller argues the rotation overshot: US staples (GSXUSTAP) trade at their richest valuation premium to the S&P in over a decade while yielding 200bps less than the 10-year Treasury, a setup after which staples underperformed in seven of nine prior cases. Miller recommends shorting staples through a binary that pays if XLP falls and 10-year swap rates fall by January 2027. Wilson separately argues rate-sensitive laggards like household appliances, auto parts, footwear and casinos have not caught up yet, pending lower rates and energy costs. October payrolls of 165K, more than double expectations, revived December rate-hike odds, threatening that catch-up trade and the rate leg of the staples short. Wilson stays in the 1998 bull camp. The author sides with Miller on staples but doubts the 1998 analogy, since that recovery came with three Fed cuts in seven weeks.
